notes.text: The page begins by saying that the envisaged arrow follows immediately. It then explicitly asks to explain how (7) and (8) result from the action on the covered set, whose fundamental-group subgroup acts freely with J as “ens quotient”. The wording “Il faudrait encore expliciter comment (7) (8) résultent” is a request for an explanation, not a proof supplied on this page.

The reformulation considers a group extension together with a nonempty set on which the extension group acts and the kernel acts freely; these systems form the category C. It then considers a connected groupoid with a universal cover and a group action, declaring a category C-prime. A small addition beside connexe remains unreadable between the supplied nonempty alternatives and is not completed from the intended mathematics.

The source announces equivalences that will be defined, quasi-inverse to one another: alpha goes from C to C-prime and beta returns from C-prime to C. No construction of these functors or proof of equivalence appears here. The tuple ends in a descending g, while the later action homomorphism is labelled with a low a; the discrepancy is preserved rather than harmonized.

Four bare shafts in the extension and the absence of a period after the first category C are preserved. The upper paragraph ends in four points. The later action homomorphism and the two bottom functor arrows do have visible arrowheads.
The page requests that the relation of (7) and (8) to the given action be made explicit. The audit reads the request as written and does not treat it as a proof supplied here.

The reformulation presents an extension and an action set whose kernel acts freely, then a groupoid with a universal cover and a group action. The first raised nonempty condition is legible; the small second insertion is not completed by analogy with it.

The tuple’s last component is a visibly descending g, while the displayed action label is a low compressed a. The difference is preserved. This explicit action-map a is a useful local graphic specimen for main’s later comparison, but no other page was inspected during this audit.

The source announces quasi-inverse equivalences alpha and beta with opposite arrow directions. Their construction is not given on this page. The audit reproduces two omitted attachment guides and otherwise preserves the accepted wording, mathematical letters, punctuation, deletions and source irregularities.

Main convention review of the existing groupoid-insertion crop confirms only a tiny loop with an upper entry and a separate short bar. The surrounding long S-like stroke is the attachment guide, not additional letters. Neither the full words non vide nor the complete signs ne-empty-set can be independently read from these surviving two graphs. The visible inscription is therefore drawn under a doubt mark; possible interpretations remain in the doubts record rather than being expanded into the transcription. This is not a mathematical correction of the groupoid condition. The different reader had independently described the same limited surviving strokes.
